metadata.purpose: Sequentially forward the original and later Observable sources, moving to the next on either completion or error.

conditions: Exactly one input is subscribed at a time; values retain identity and order within an input.
Either completion or error of a current input starts the next supplied source.
When the final input completes or errors, emit a normal result completion; never emit an error notification.

scope.parameters: Pipeable deprecated onErrorResumeNext alias of onErrorResumeNextWith; 2 other valid Observable sources, no promises or iterables.
scope.callbacks: No callbacks or inspection of error values. Error details are intentionally discarded.
scope.time: Only active source notifications determine time; no timer. Sequential resource acquisition is synchronous in each terminal reaction.
scope.reentrancy: Atomic nonreentrant source terminal steps and subscription acquisition.
exclusions: Synchronous reentrant emission during subscription acquisition; arbitrary ObservableInput conversions and conversion throws.
Unbounded argument counts over 32; any user observer callback reentry or throwing teardown.

initialization.sourceSubscription: Subscribe source at input index 0; other inputs wait for previous termination.

ownership.sharing: No sharing; one input active per result subscription.
ownership.reset: Each result execution starts at index 0 and forgets earlier errors.

resources.owner: current result, generation is fixed source position

dispatch.actionSemantics: Current input terminal tears down its subscription before acquiring next. Error is never forwarded.
cancellationCheckpoints: Between notifications; unsubscribe current and discard pending inputs.

rules.explanation: The pipeable export subscribes the original source first and defers every later source.
Only the currently subscribed input may contribute next values.

rules.guard: current input terminal and one later input remains
rules.explanation: Both completion and error advance to the next input; errors are deliberately swallowed.
An error from the last input also produces normal completion, never an output error.
